key: I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals. On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother.
s: In a hymn to Agni Vaisvanara as fire and Sun, the singer turns to two roads; Sāyaṇa, on 10.88.15, reads them as the gods’ way and the fathers’ way, by which all between heaven and earth, hallowed by fire, goes to those worlds.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.88.15, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 363752 (2022)

evidence.gloss: Of the fathers and the gods, and of mortals, men too: two paths, two roads named the way of the gods and the way of the fathers, I have heard. Whatever all there is between the father, heaven, a father because it protects, and the mother, earth, a mother because it upholds, that is in the middle of heaven and earth: this all, made ready by fire, moving, going to the world of the gods and the world of the fathers, goes by those two roads named the way of the gods and the way of the fathers.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 10.88.15, at [924,15]); hymn 10.88 praises Agni as fire at night and Sun at morn (10.88.6, 11) and as Vaisvanara (12 to 14); the context clause repeats none of the verse. Sāyaṇa on 10.88.15 (packet, sa.wikisource rev 363752) names the two paths devayāna and pitṛyāṇa and says all that lies between heaven the father and earth the mother, prepared (saṃskṛta) by fire, goes by them to the world of the gods and the world of the fathers; the sentence carries this without addition (‘hallowed’ renders saṃskṛta in its ritual sense). Wilson’s note confirms he cites Gita 8.24 to 26 on the two paths. Nirukta does not treat the verse. Evidence re-found by machine in the packet text. entry-check ok.
